mechanism: Palace Model.Refinement.Boxes on the EXISTING mesh; no gmsh, no new mesh file
candidate_mesh_sha256: identical to baseline; the mesh file is an input, not regenerated

refinement_region.justification: the lumped-port face (attribute 10) bounding box padded by 0.010 mm, the same pad R1 declared. NOTE: the same pad does NOT make the perturbation comparable in size -- R1 added 818 DOF, while this candidate's LOWER bound alone is +1920, at least 2.3x, before any green closure. The pad is shared for continuity of the declared region, not to match the perturbation magnitude.

marking.criterion: any vertex of the element inside the closed box (geodata.cpp:282-306)
marking.accounting_gap: boundary elements are bisected too, and Palace adds 9449 interface boundary elements at load; neither appears in the 221/64434 element count. Edge count is unaffected.

dof.why_not_measured: the refined mesh exists only inside Palace at load time. MFEM has no Python binding in this environment and Palace's --dry-run parses the config only (main.cpp:246-254), so no offline measurement is possible without reimplementing MFEM's bisection.
dof.lower_bound_derivation: marked submesh refines uniformly (octasection): E' = 2E+3F+T. Green closure only ADDS elements (mesh.cpp:10123), so E_total >= E_baseline + E(M) + 3F(M) + T(M).
dof.upper_bound_note: uniform refinement of the whole mesh; 2.46x the budget. There is no tighter upper bound available offline, so the honest offline statement is the interval [81864, 615486].
dof.breach_argument: breaching 250000 from 79944 needs 170056 added edges; the marked octasection supplies 1920 and a full uniform refinement supplies 535542, so a breach requires the green closure to deliver 31.8% of a uniform refinement -- an 89x expansion of the 221 marked elements. Computable offline; still not a measurement.
dof.enforcement: Palace prints 'ND (p = 1)' at palace_log.txt line 49, before the eigensolver is configured at line 54. The gate is enforceable by a probe that reads that line and kills the job, with seconds of exposure -- NOT by degrading the rule to a post-hoc check.

invariants_by_construction.mesh_file: byte-identical; refinement is a config block
invariants_by_construction.existing_vertex_coordinates: never moved; new vertices are edge midpoints only (mesh.cpp:10834-10841)
invariants_by_construction.port_connectivity_and_L_s: w and l come from mesh::GetBoundingBox on the port attribute (lumpedelement.cpp:22-69). That box is ORIENTED, not axis-aligned (geodata.hpp:124-128). Midpoints are convex combinations so no inserted vertex can become a new extremum; the extremal-point selection is tie-broken by list order and refinement reorders the cloud, but axes are re-sorted by descending length (geodata.cpp:1013-1014), so Lengths() is permutation-invariant. Safe for THIS rectangular planar port; not a general guarantee.
invariants_by_construction.Lc: computed from the PRE-refinement bounding box: main.cpp:311-313 orders ReadMesh -> NondimensionalizeInputs -> RefineMesh, and iodata.cpp:448-463 runs under MFEM_VERIFY(!init). Lc cannot see the refinement at all.

propagation.why: GeneralRefinement forces nonconforming=0 for 3D simplex meshes (mesh.cpp:10565-10567)
propagation.beyond_the_region: YES. ParMesh::LocalRefinement (pmesh.cpp:3385) restores conformity by bisecting ANY element needing it, marked or not (pmesh.cpp:3467-3477), with an MPI face exchange (3489-3560) and boundary elements (3568-3580). This is NOT a face-only or box-only change, and its extent is not computable offline.
propagation.MaxNCLevels_and_Nonconformal: inert for tets; the conforming branch is taken first

quality.note: octasection of a tet is not quality-preserving in general; bisection quality is bounded by MFEM's marked-edge scheme but is not measured here
